items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: This trio has kind of evolved into the Rossano Sportiello Trio. You know Nicki will front it, or sometimes I will front it, it’s kind of Rossano’s band.

ctx.x: He plays soft, it’s unbelievable. And so Nicki and I try to capture that with him. Like all of a sudden, we’ll be playing something loud, and then the bottom just drops out. But yet

the intensity of the beat continues. And that’s a really difficult thing to do in music. I think it’s the hardest thing to do in music. I used to hear that with Oscar Peterson records, trio records with Ray Brown and Ed Thigpen. They’d be playing and all of a sudden the bottom would drop out and Oscar might be just playing one note. But the beat continued through. And that’s what really impressed me.

items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: We had some in May, nice concerts, a couple of nice concerts we were supposed to do in May in Florida.

ctx.x: Do you have booked gigs with Rossano and Eddie?

Yeah we lost some. Yup. We had some in May, nice concerts, a couple of nice concerts we were supposed to do in May in Florida. A couple of jazz parties and hopefully December in Bern, Switzerland. We’ll see if Marians in Bern is opened up. That’s a beautiful club. I hope that happens.
What does it do to your identity?
